title: Two Teams

source.name: Original exercise; classic technique (bipartite check by 2-colouring)

statement:
There are `n` students numbered `1` to `n` and `m` pairs of students who dislike each other. Can you split all students into two teams so that no pair of students who dislike each other end up in the same team? (A team may be empty.)

**Input.** First line: `n` and `m`. Then `m` lines `a b`. A pair may appear several times, and a student may even dislike themselves (`a a`).

**Output.** `YES` if such a split exists, otherwise `NO`.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 4000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 8000 in this browser version (the idea scales to 2·10^5)
hints: Pick any student and put them in team 0. Who is forced into team 1? And then who is forced back into team 0?
Run a BFS and give each newly reached student the opposite colour of the one that reached them. Every other edge must then join different colours.

If an edge joins two students of the same colour, the answer is NO (there is an odd cycle). Start a new BFS from every uncoloured student: the graph may be disconnected, and a self-loop is such a conflicting edge.
editorial: A graph can be split into two teams exactly when it is **bipartite**, which holds exactly when it has no cycle of odd length. A breadth-first search colours each vertex with the opposite colour of its discoverer. Within one connected component the colours are forced, so any edge between two equally coloured vertices proves an odd cycle, and if no such edge exists the colouring is a valid split. Each component needs its own search because isolated or separate groups are not reached from vertex `1`. Time `O(n + m)`. Parallel edges are harmless and a self-loop immediately conflicts, because a vertex has the same colour as itself.

starter.python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n, m = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
# pairs start at data[2]: a b

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import deque
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n, m = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for i in range(m):
    a, b = int(data[2 + 2 * i]), int(data[3 + 2 * i])
    adj[a].append(b)
    adj[b].append(a)
color = [-1] * (n + 1)
ok = True
for s in range(1, n + 1):         # the graph may have several components
    if color[s] != -1:
        continue
    color[s] = 0
    q = deque([s])
    while q and ok:
        u = q.popleft()
        for v in adj[u]:
            if color[v] == -1:
                color[v] = color[u] ^ 1
                q.append(v)
            elif color[v] == color[u]:   # an edge inside one side: an odd cycle
                ok = False
                break
    if not ok:
        break
print("YES" if ok else "NO")
